newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Adelaide Brighton says profit ahead.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Adelaide Brighton says profit ahead.

text.p: Adelaide Brighton Ltd said on Wednesday profit was about 10 percent up on last year for the first four months of 1996/97, despite weaker cement demand.

"As a result of the relentless downward pressure on costs, group profit is running about 10 percent ahead of last year for the first four months of trading, despite weaker demand for cement," chairman Rodney White told the annual meeting.

"With the return to more normal weather patterns during hte summer months directors stand by their prediction that operating profits for this financial year are likely to show a modest improvement over 1995," White said.
White said the company saw no signs yet of any improvement in demand for its products.
"In fact, cement sales have continued to decline slightly from the previous year," he said.

White said reduced economic activity in the building and construction sector had pushed sales lower, but added that there was some evidence that weaker demand so far in 1996/97 had been exacerbated by extended wet weather, particularly throughout southern Australia.
"Our best estimate for market demand for the products we produce is that demand has bottomed out and that, in fact, a slight improvement should emerge during calendar 1997," he said.
Adelaide Brighton made a loss of A$49.26 million in the year to June 30, 1996, after abnormal losses of A$22.9 million.
Adelaide Brighton shares were steady at A$1.74 at 11.55 a.m. (0055 GMT).
